title: Why this reply is written
source_text: Καὶ ἀληθῶς ἄξιον μὲν ἡμᾶς σεμνύνεσθαι ἐπὶ θλίψει μὴ χωριζούσῃ ἢ τοῖς ἑξῆς αὐτῇ κατειλεγμένοις, οὐχὶ δὲ Παῦλον καὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους. καὶ εἴ τις ἐκείνοις γέγονε παραπλήσιος, διὰ τὸ πάνυ ὑπεράνω τῶν τοιούτων εἶναι λέγοντα τό· „ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς·“ ὅπερ μεῖζόν ἐστι τοῦ νικᾶν. εἰ δὲ δεῖ καὶ ἀποστόλους σεμνύνεσθαι. μὴ χωριζομένους „ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν“, σεμνύνοιντο ἂν, „ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ, οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ“ οὔτε τι τῶν ἑξῆς δύναται αὐτοὺς „χωρίσαι (ἀπὸ) τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν“. τοίνυν οὐ συνήδομαι τῷ πιστεύσαντι εἰς Χριστὸν, ὡς δύνασθαι σαλευθῆναι αὐτοῦ τὴν πίστιν ὑπὸ Κέλσου, τοῦ οὐδὲ κοινοτέραν ζωὴν ζῶντος ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἔτι ἀλλ᾿ ἤδη καὶ πάλαι νεκροῦ, ἤ τινος πιθανότητος λόγου. οὐκ οἶδα δ᾿ ἐν ποίῳ τάγματι λογίσασθαι χρὴ τὸν δεόμενον λόγων πρὸς τὰ Κέλσου κατὰ Χριστιανῶν ἐγκλήματα ἐν βίβλοις ἀναγραφομένων. ἀποκαθιστάντων αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν πίστιν σεισμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆναι ἐν αὐτῇ. ὅμως δ᾿ ἐπεὶ ἐν τῷ πλήθει τῶν πιστεύειν νομιζομένων εὑρεθεῖεν ἄν τινες τοιοῦτοι, ὡς σαλεύεσθαι μὲν καὶ ἀνατρέπεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν Κέλσου γραμμάτων θεραπεύεσθαι δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς πρὸς αὐτὰ ἀπολογίας, ἐὰν ἔχῃ χαρακτῆρά τινα καθαιρετικὸν τῶν Κέλσου καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας παραστατικὸν τὰ λεγόμενα, ἐλογισάμεθα πεισθῆναί σου τῇ προστάξει καὶ ὑπαγορεῦσαι πρὸς ὃ ἔπεμψας ἡμῖν σύγγραμμα· ὅπερ οὐκ οἶμαί τινα τῶν ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ κἂν ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον προκοψάντων συγκαταθέσθαι εἶναι λόγον ἀληθῆ, ὡς ἐπέγραψεν ὁ Κέλσος.
pass_a_gloss: And truly it is fitting (ἄξιον) for us to take pride (σεμνύνομαι) at affliction (θλῖψις) not separating (χωρίζω), or at the things listed next after it, but not for Paul and the apostles (ἀπόστολοι), and if anyone has become like (παραπλήσιος) them, because of being entirely above (ὑπεράνω) such things, saying (λέγοντα, acc. sg.): [Rom 8:37: in all these we more-than-conquer (ὑπερνικάω) through the one who loved us]; which is greater than conquering (νικάω). But if apostles too must take pride in not being separated 'from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord', they would take pride (opt.) 'that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities' nor any of what follows is able to 'separate them from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord'. Therefore I do not rejoice with (συνήδομαι) the one who has believed in Christ so that his faith (πίστις) can be shaken (σαλεύω) by Celsus, who no longer lives even a more common (κοινότερος) life among men but is already and long since dead (νεκρός), or by some plausibility (πιθανότης) of argument (λόγος). I do not know in what rank (τάγμα) one must reckon (λογίζομαι) the one needing arguments recorded (ἀναγράφω) in books against Celsus's charges (ἐγκλήματα) against Christians, restoring (ἀποκαθίστημι) him from the shaking (σεισμός) regarding the faith to standing (ἵστημι) in it. Yet since in the multitude of those thought (νομίζω) to believe some such might be found as to be shaken and overturned (ἀνατρέπω) by Celsus's writings (γράμματα) but healed (θεραπεύω) by the defence (ἀπολογία) against them, if the things said have some character (χαρακτήρ) destructive (καθαιρετικός) of Celsus's [claims] and presentative (παραστατικός) of the truth (ἀλήθεια), we reckoned to obey your command (πρόσταξις) and dictate (ὑπαγορεύω) toward the treatise (σύγγραμμα) you sent us; which I do not think anyone of those who have advanced (προκόπτω) in philosophy (φιλοσοφία) even a little would agree (συγκατατίθημι) is a 'true word/doctrine' (λόγος ἀληθής), as Celsus entitled (ἐπιγράφω) it.
pass_b_english: And truly it is fitting for us to take pride in affliction that does not separate us, or in the things listed after it; but not for Paul and the apostles, or for anyone who has become like them. For one who says, “In all these things we more than conquer through him who loved us” (Romans 8:37), is far above such things; and that is greater than conquering. And if apostles too must take pride in not being separated “from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 8:39), they would take pride that “neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities,” nor any of the things that follow, is able “to separate” them “from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 8:38–39).

So I take no joy in a believer in Christ whose faith could be shaken by Celsus, a man who no longer lives even the common life among men but is already long dead, or by any plausible argument. And I do not know in what rank one ought to count someone who needs arguments set down in books against Celsus’s charges against Christians, to bring him back from wavering in his faith to standing firm in it.

Yet among the multitude of those who are thought to believe, some might be found of such a kind as to be shaken and overturned by Celsus’s writings, but healed by a defence against them, if what is said has a character that demolishes Celsus’s claims and sets forth the truth. For this reason we have decided to obey your command and to dictate a reply to the treatise you sent us. I do not think that anyone who has made even a little progress in philosophy would grant that this treatise is a “True Doctrine,” as Celsus entitled it.

choices.choice: 'σεμνύνεσθαι ἐπὶ θλίψει μὴ χωριζούσῃ' (to take pride at an affliction not separating) is rendered 'to take pride when affliction does not separate us'. 'λέγοντα' (acc. sg.) refers most naturally to Paul as speaker of Rom 8:37, extended to anyone like him; rendered 'such a one ... since he says'. 'οὐ συνήδομαι τῷ πιστεύσαντι ... ὡς δύνασθαι σαλευθῆναι' rendered 'I take no joy in a believer ... whose faith could be shaken'. 'τοῦ οὐδὲ κοινοτέραν ζωὴν ζῶντος ... ἀλλ᾿ ἤδη καὶ πάλαι νεκροῦ' refers to Celsus being long dead; kept literal. 'λόγον ἀληθῆ, ὡς ἐπέγραψεν' plays on the title of Celsus's book (Λόγος ἀληθής), rendered 'True Doctrine' to match the title used on Via Patrum; the title is Celsus's own wording, hence double quotation marks. The edition's stray full stops ('σεμνύνεσθαι. μὴ', 'ἀναγραφομένων. ἀποκαθιστάντων') are ignored. The parenthetical '(ἀπὸ)' is Koetschau's supplement, matching Rom 8:39; translated. No LXX renumbering needed.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.

changes: 'it would be fitting' -> 'it is fitting' (ἄξιον with no ἄν; modality corrected)
'take pride when affliction does not separate us, or any of the things' -> 'take pride in affliction that does not separate us, or in the things' (ἐπὶ θλίψει μὴ χωριζούσῃ ἢ τοῖς ἑξῆς)

'For such a one is far above such things, since he says' -> 'For one who says ... is far above such things' (διὰ τὸ ... εἶναι λέγοντα: the speaker of Romans 8:37 is the one above them; 'since' made his saying the cause)
'their pride would be that' -> 'they would take pride that' (σεμνύνοιντο ἄν); the split quotation from Romans 8:38-39 now carries one citation (Romans 8:38-39) instead of two
'in what rank to count' -> 'in what rank one ought to count' (χρή)
Straight apostrophes made curly to match the rest of the file

source_ref: Koetschau GCS 2 (1899), Contra Celsum, Preface 4, via the Perseus TEI
